name: Marxist–Leninist atheism
summary: Marxist–Leninist atheism is the antireligious part of Marxism–Leninism, which treats religion as an illusion produced by exploitation and insecurity and holds that atheism is part of a communist's worldview. Lenin asked the state to treat religion as private and separate from the church, while the Party itself carries on materialist and atheist propaganda tied to the class struggle. In power, communist states pursued official atheism through closures of places of worship, antireligious education and persecution of clergy and believers.
scope: The doctrine of religion in Marx, Engels and Lenin (Marx's 1843 Introduction, Lenin's 'Socialism and Religion', 'The Attitude of the Workers' Party to Religion' and 'On the Significance of Militant Materialism') and its use as 'scientific atheism' in the Soviet Union. Answers on topics beyond religion are inferred from the parent doctrine of Marxism–Leninism and are marked low. Later reforms in Vietnam, Laos and Cuba, liberation theology and religious-left Marxism are excluded.

keyFigures.name: Vladimir Lenin
keyFigures.role: Set the Party's line on religion and militant atheism in 1905, 1909 and 1922.

keyFigures.name: Karl Marx
keyFigures.role: Authored the critique of religion as an illusion of oppressed people ('opium of the people').

universal-healthcare.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states guaranteed free medical care as part of the socialist programme; the religion-focused sources do not discuss health policy, so this is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Lenin ties the fight against religion to workers' economic struggle against capital, which implies backing higher wages, though no text addresses minimum-wage law.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Marxist–Leninist doctrine opposes market allocation under capitalism; the atheism sources never address it, so the answer is inferred from the parent doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Public ownership of major industry is a core of the Marxism–Leninism that this atheism belongs to, but none of the opened sources discusses it directly.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the anti-capitalist class orientation Lenin gives the movement in 1909; no source discusses tax rates.

unions-good.rationale: Lenin treats strikes and workers' organisation as the place where unity matters most, so unions are favoured, but this is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Marx's critique moves from religion to law and politics, and Marxism rejects property as an untouchable right; inferred, not stated in these sources.

regulate-corporations.rationale: A Marxist–Leninist would see tighter regulation as at best a half-measure towards ownership; inferred from the parent doctrine, so low confidence.

cut-welfare.rationale: Lenin's concern with workers' material insecurity as the root of religion implies opposing welfare cuts; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Marxist–Leninist practice favours state over cooperative ownership, so the answer leans negative; no source here covers the point.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Soviet-type states that enforced atheism relied on security organs, but no source here addresses counter-terror surveillance specifically.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by any opened source; inferred from the moralising public-health stance of Marxist–Leninist states.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states restricted speech seen as reactionary, though the sources here cover only religion, so the answer is inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Marxist–Leninist rule is by a party rather than by a single leader bypassing institutions, so a mild yes at most; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Marx's criticism of religion extends to criticism of the state as an inverted world, but a Marxist–Leninist keeps the state during the transition; inferred.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in any opened source; adherents are split between workers' arming and state monopoly of force.

empower-police-military.rationale: The sources do not address police funding; the state is treated as a class instrument, so a mild no is inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states treated prostitution as a capitalist evil; inferred from the parent doctrine.

decide-locally.rationale: Democratic centralism points away from local autonomy; inferred, as no source here treats it.

rehabilitation.rationale: Soviet penal doctrine stressed re-education, but this is inferred as the sources are about religion.

traditional-family.rationale: Marxist–Leninist atheism treated religious family traditions as outdated; the family's role is not discussed in the opened sources, so low.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states historically did not recognise it and it is not discussed here; low-confidence inference.

abortion-legal.rationale: The Soviet Union legalised abortion and religious opposition was dismissed, but the sources opened do not state this.

more-religion-public.rationale: Lenin demands complete separation of church and state and a materialist worldview, and the official atheist states closed places of worship, so a larger public role for religion is firmly rejected.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed by the religion sources; inferred from Marxist–Leninist anti-racism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed here; Marxist emphasis on social conditions shaping people suggests a lean agree.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Marxist–Leninist atheism treated church-bound national traditions as superstition to be outgrown, so only a mild yes is inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Lenin ties the end of religion to the overthrow of capitalism rather than gradual reform, but the statement is about institutions in general, so inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; internationalist Marxist–Leninism leans against restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed by these sources; inferred as ambivalent leaning negative towards bourgeois-led bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed here; Marxist–Leninist doctrine opposes capitalist free trade.

nation-first.rationale: The religion sources do not discuss it; proletarian internationalism leans against national self-interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Marxist–Leninists treat such interventions as imperialist pretexts.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed in the religion sources; internationalism gives a weak lean to agree.

limit-growth.rationale: Marxist–Leninist doctrine favours productive development; the sources here do not address growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; a planned-economy tradition makes state action plausible, so a weak lean agree.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Lenin's call for scientific materialism and alliance with natural scientists suggests faith in science, but technology and social problems are not discussed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed in any opened source; inferred from Soviet industrial policy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Lenin links the end of religion to the revolutionary struggle against capital, so revolution is justified, but only inferentially from these religion texts.

experts-over-public.rationale: Lenin urges alliance with natural scientists and scientific authority, but the statement concerns policy-making generally, so inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning is part of the parent doctrine; no opened source here discusses it.

socialized-markets.rationale: Marxist–Leninists are split between planning only and market socialism; the sources here are silent.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Marxist–Leninists would favour abolishing private land ownership instead.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed here; inferred from hostility to inherited wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states tied support to work, so an unconditional income is rejected; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed by these sources; state protection of industry is consistent with the parent doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of investment is part of the parent doctrine, not a point these religion sources cover.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Marxism favours social ownership over small-owner property; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolition of money and wages is a long-run Marxist aim, not discussed in the opened sources.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed here; Marxist–Leninists would nationalise banking, not leave money to markets.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; class struggle rather than tripartite bargaining is the Marxist–Leninist frame.

one-party-rule.rationale: Lenin's Party must be unified on a materialist worldview and treats religion differently from the state, but the single-party state itself is not discussed in these texts.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The sources describe the church as a Tsarist ally that Lenin attacked together with the monarchy, so hereditary monarchy is rejected.

democracy-best.rationale: Marxist–Leninists distinguish bourgeois from proletarian democracy; the sources do not give a direct answer.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed here; inferred from democratic centralism.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviets are central to the parent doctrine, not to the religion sources.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lenin's national programme supports self-determination, but it is not addressed in the religion texts opened.

natural-rulers.rationale: Lenin's materialism treats human ideas, including religion, as products of social conditions rather than innate fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Marxist–Leninists accept revolutionary violence; the sources opened document anti-religious violence only in Soviet practice.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Marxist–Leninists treat war as a product of capitalism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Lenin's 1905 article demands complete separation of church and state, no state funds for churches and no official record of belief.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Lenin treats religion as a private matter for the state and demands that law not carry any religious establishment.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the state is treated as the public instrument of force.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Soviet-style states prized military strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Marxism–Leninism opposes ethnic definition of the nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Lenin insists the fight against religion must be tied to class struggle, which he treats as the driving force.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from communist distribution aims.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from anti-colonial Leninism.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from anti-imperialism.

civilizational-union.rationale: Marxist–Leninist atheism rejects union based on religion; the broader point is inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Marx treats egoistic illusion critically, but the question of morality of self-interest is not addressed directly.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Soviet doctrine stressed duties alongside rights; inferred, not stated in these sources.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; a materialist philosophy values nature through human use.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; Marxists reject Malthusian limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marxism treats industrial capitalism as progressive; not covered by the sources opened.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Lenin's alliance with natural scientists suggests support for scientific progress, but disruptive acceleration is not discussed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; scientific optimism gives a weak lean to agree.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed in any source; adherents have no settled view.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; states of this kind favoured state access to communications.

restore-past-order.rationale: Lenin's critique casts religion as a relic of exploitative conditions to be overcome, rejecting restoration of a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Lenin demands militant materialist philosophy as the guide of practice, which implies ideology over pragmatism; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Lenin favours organised class action but criticises anarchist 'war on God' tactics, so direct action alone is only weakly supported.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; Leninists accept coercive means for socialist ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marx looks forward to people taking control of their conditions through history, not returning to a primitive state.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolition of the division of labour is a Marxist aim not covered by these sources.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The need-based principle is part of the parent doctrine; no opened source states it.

production-for-use.rationale: Part of the parent doctrine and not discussed in the religion sources.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Lenin roots religion in the insecurity capitalism imposes on workers, which presupposes exploitation, but profit theory is not stated here.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Part of the parent doctrine; not addressed in the opened religion sources.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed here; Soviet practice was collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; part of the Leninist theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; Marxists reject the view that taxation is theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist–Leninist states restricted private conduct beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist–Leninists treat rights as class-conditioned.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Soviet states used universal conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; emigration was restricted in Soviet-type states.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; the state is a class instrument, not a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marx says abolishing illusory happiness means demanding real happiness and the means for it, consistent with material freedom, though not explicit.

media-academia-power.rationale: Lenin calls bourgeois philosophy professors 'flunkeys of clericalism', but the claim about media power over elected officials is not made.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Marx's view that man makes religion and conditions shape ideas implies environmental explanations; race is not discussed.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; corporatist representation is opposed to class politics.

total-state.rationale: Official atheist states sought to direct culture and education, per the article, but total direction of every area is inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist–Leninism rejects nationalist rebirth myths.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Lenin links the church to Tsarist authority and rejects such feudal bonds, but not directly on this question.

bound-labor.rationale: Lenin's programme calls for freeing the exploited, and bonded labour is a feudal remnant he attacks.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Lenin calls bourgeois philosophy professors 'flunkeys of clericalism', treating academic philosophy as serving class interests, a partial match to the claim.

universal-morality.rationale: Marxist atheism grounds morality in class, but the sources only touch on morality in passing.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist–Leninists see politics as class interest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the opened sources; Soviet doctrine was anti-Zionist.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no settled view.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred as indifferent to mildly negative.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed here; Soviet practice favoured party and state management.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist–Leninists favour state-run schools, as the atheism curriculum shows.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The atheism doctrine says nothing on fiscal policy; a state-planning tradition makes austerity-minded balanced budgets unlikely to be a priority, so a mild disagree.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist–Leninists reject the claim.

rule-by-example.rationale: Soviet atheism relied on law, party discipline and propaganda rather than rulers' moral example, so a mild disagree is inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed in the religion sources; Leninist doctrine supports it.

force-without-un.rationale: Not a topic of the atheism texts; Soviet-bloc states acted without UN approval when it suited them, so a weak agree is inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Lenin calls the fight against religion the ABC of materialism and demands militant scientific materialism, so reason over faith is central.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Internationalist doctrine tilts against nationality-based welfare limits, but the religion sources never raise it.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed here; Soviet ethos stressed that those who do not work shall not eat.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lenin says atheist propaganda must be subordinated to class struggle and that dividing strikers into believers and atheists helps the bourgeoisie.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Soviets turned churches into museums or warehouses, but sacrificing libraries and museums is not stated.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialist alliances are part of Leninism generally; the religion-centred sources do not discuss them, so a weak agree.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed here; internationalism opposes national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist–Leninists opposed legal gender-role distinctions.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Marxist–Leninists did not ban interest on religious grounds.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Marxist–Leninism treats racial segregation as an instrument of class rule; inferred from the parent doctrine, not from the religion sources.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The article reports Lenin seeing the church as serving the state; the general theory is part of the parent doctrine.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Soviet-type states expanded fossil-fuel output as part of industrialisation; the atheism sources do not discuss energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Soviet practice promoted a common socialist culture without demanding ethnic assimilation; the topic is outside the atheism texts.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not covered by any source; Marxist–Leninists explain migration through labour markets and reject such conspiracies, so a mild disagree.

proportional-representation.rationale: Marxist–Leninists favoured soviet-style delegation over party-list parliaments; inferred, since the sources do not discuss electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: Soviet doctrine claimed a universal socialist mission, so a weak agree is inferred; the atheism texts themselves are silent.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Marxist feminism supports it mildly.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Lenin's account of religion as a tool of the ruling class implies elite complicity, but corruption of political elites is not discussed.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Marxist materialism stressed environment over heredity, so eugenic limits are mildly rejected; nothing in the sources states it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The atheism sources record repression by the security organs without any accountability doctrine; adherents lean against it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Not addressed; rejected by Marxist–Leninist doctrine.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Marxist–Leninist internationalism rejects racial separation; this is inferred and not stated in the religion sources.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Lenin demands that the law not discriminate between citizens by belief or disbelief, supporting equal rights, though at a general level.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Stalinist doctrine says one country suffices.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial Leninism generally treats settler states as colonial projects, but the point is not covered by the sources opened.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Lenin demands equal law for all citizens regardless of religion, with no official record of belief.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Lenin demands freedom to profess any religion, but Soviet practice limited religious propaganda; adherents are split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; religious dietary law is not a basis for state law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Soviet state barred private religious instruction of minors and taught scientific atheism, so religious instruction in state schools is rejected.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Stalinist thesis that the state grows stronger under encirclement belongs to the parent doctrine; the atheism sources do not discuss it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Marxist–Leninists ground legitimacy in the working class led by the party, not individual consent; inferred rather than stated.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not covered by the sources; Soviet planning aimed at self-sufficiency rather than export surpluses, so a mild disagree.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the article does not cover forced population movement.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Marxist–Leninists accept revolutionary force, and the sources describe state coercion against religion, so the statement is rejected by inference.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Marxist doctrine ascribes progress to class struggle and material development rather than competition between individuals or peoples; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Soviet-type states banned parties opposing the socialist order, but the religion sources do not state the principle.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Marx's call to end the conditions that need illusions fits an anti-domination idea of freedom, though not a republican-theory one.

separated-powers.rationale: Soviet doctrine placed power in unified soviets under party leadership; separation of powers was rejected, as inferred from the parent doctrine.

vanguard-party.rationale: Lenin treats the party as the conscious guide that educates religious workers into its programme, but the vanguard theory is not stated here.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Lenin's concern with the oppressed as the people religion consoles suggests priority for the poor, though not about institutions.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Marxist–Leninist housing policy favoured public rather than private ownership; inferred, not stated in the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Lenin values strike unity, so restricting strikes is rejected.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Lenin says poverty and insecurity come from capitalist exploitation, not from population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Lenin argues that dividing workers by belief weakens them and unity matters most, which counters a diversity-cohesion worry.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Soviet practice used party nomination and election, so lotteries are mildly rejected by inference.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The article shows Soviet states suspending legal protections for believers, but a general emergency doctrine is inferred only.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Fixed prices were part of Soviet economic management; the sources opened say nothing on food prices.

party-controls-media.rationale: The article notes that Soviet states used propaganda and censorship against religion, but media control generally is not covered.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the armed forces was Soviet practice through political commissars; the religion sources do not discuss it.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Marxist–Leninism has no set doctrine; internationalism favours easier citizenship, so a mild disagree, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The workers'-pay principle for officials comes from the Paris Commune tradition Lenin adopted; the religion sources do not discuss it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Lenin lets the party expel those who make religious propaganda their main work, showing discipline, but the statement is general.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Marxist–Leninists criticise the EU as a capitalist bloc; no opened source discusses supranational unions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Soviet doctrine placed command in party and collective organs rather than a single head of state; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Lenin treats the church as a private association of believers, so its internal form is not the state's concern; hierarchy is disfavoured.

clerical-rule.rationale: Lenin treats the church as a tool of Tsarist oppression and demands separation, so clerical political authority is firmly rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's revolutionary-defeatist line in imperialist war belongs to his other writings; the atheism texts do not address it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The article describes anti-religious censorship in Soviet states, supporting a weak agree, but virtue-based censorship is not stated.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states differed, with some party leaders ruling for decades; adherents are split.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of delegates is a soviet principle Lenin endorsed in State and Revolution, but the atheism sources do not mention it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states built their own alliances such as the Warsaw Pact, so ending permanent alliances is mildly rejected.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Soviet policy favoured state-owned rental housing, so the abolition of renting is mildly rejected; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The armed-people idea appears in Lenin's wider writing, but Soviet states kept standing armies; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; peasants were viewed as religious and backward.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states supported reunification on socialist terms, as with Korea or Vietnam; the sources opened do not state it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Lenin treats the educated as needed allies, though he calls professors lackeys of clericalism, so out of touch is not the view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The atheism doctrine ranks scientific materialism above religious worldviews, but the statement concerns civilisations, so a weak agree.

death-penalty.rationale: Soviet-type states retained execution, and the article records executions of clergy; adherents likely agree, though no source states a general principle.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not covered by the sources, but state-run secular schooling suggests agreement with modern curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Scientific atheism was grounded in dialectical materialism and taught as science, so creationism in schools is firmly rejected.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Soviet states banned pornography as bourgeois decadence, so a weak agree is inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states had no settled doctrine and the sources do not discuss it, so adherents are split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Soviet nationalities policy supported minority languages in schools, but this is outside the atheism sources.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Lenin demands equality of citizens whatever their belief, so special exemptions are disfavoured, but the point is not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states pressed conformity to a scientific worldview, so a mild disagree is inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialist doctrine supports cancelling poor countries' debts, but the sources opened do not discuss debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Leninist theory of imperialism says independence without economic change is formal; not covered by the atheism sources.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Bolsheviks dissolved the Constituent Assembly in 1918, so adherents mildly reject it; the sources opened do not mention it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states justified limits on freedom for socialist construction; the sources opened do not state the principle.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Marxist–Leninists hold that rich countries owe poor ones as a matter of anti-imperial justice; not covered by the religion sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Soviet and Chinese states built independent deterrents; inferred, not stated in the sources.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states chose heads of state through assemblies rather than direct election, so a mild disagree.

central-bank-independence.rationale: State control of banking is basic to the parent doctrine, so independence from government is rejected; not covered here.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Marxist–Leninism does not hold the historic-homeland view, so adherents mildly disagree; not covered by the sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Socialist doctrine subordinates property to social ownership, so agreement is inferred; the sources opened do not state it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents treat the USSR as socialist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Planning traditions favour state action against risks, but no source here discusses environmental risk.

collective-defense.rationale: Warsaw Pact states adopted collective-defence clauses, so a weak agree is inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Leninist self-determination implies annexation without consent is unlawful, though the sources opened do not say so.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Lenin demands that no funds go to churches and the Soviet state closed places of worship and placed clergy under state control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Marxist–Leninist heads of state were party leaders, so a nonpartisan symbolic head is mildly rejected.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Marxist–Leninists are split between the Leninist right to secede and Soviet practice of preventing it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states resisted separate systems within a state, though China's 'one country, two systems' is an exception; weak disagree.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The article describes Lenin tying religious credibility to the Tsar's legitimacy and rejecting it, so a sacred ruler is rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Socialist doctrine favours progressive taxation, so a flat rate is mildly rejected by inference.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marx says man makes religion and the conditions of the world produce illusions, treating belief as formed by circumstances.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Marxist–Leninists treat law as class instrument and the party as the ruler, so the statement is mildly rejected as framed.

space-expansion.rationale: The Soviet Union prized space achievement as a socialist triumph, so a weak agree; the sources opened do not discuss it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Marxist–Leninists reject mixed regimes that preserve elite power; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; cults of leaders appeared in Soviet states.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and there is no settled doctrine, so a weak disagree from Soviet family law is inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Lenin ties atheist propaganda to class struggle, but the doctrine of continuing struggle under socialism belongs to Stalin and Mao; adherents here mildly disagree.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; church lands were also seized.

refugee-return.rationale: No settled doctrine and the sources are silent, so adherents are split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Leninism rejects irredentist claims based on nationality of residents; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Lenin condemns laws that persecute people for belief or disbelief and asks for leaving religion to be free.

common-currency.rationale: Marxist–Leninists criticised the euro as capitalist, so a mild disagree; the sources opened do not address currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Proletarian internationalism rejects union on ancestry, so a mild disagree is inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Lenin opposed Bundist national-cultural autonomy in favour of territorial autonomy; this is not in the atheism sources, so low confidence.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Lenin's call to unite workers regardless of belief supports minorities fighting for equality where they live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marx and Lenin root religion in social and economic conditions and insist change comes by transforming them rather than by criticism alone.

ban-cartels.rationale: Marxist–Leninists see monopolies as a stage of capitalism to be socialised rather than broken up, so a mild disagree.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not covered by the sources; Marxist–Leninism opposes bailouts of capital but favours state takeover, so a mild disagree.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Soviet doctrine made courts instruments of the people's power, so adherents mildly agree.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Soviet states set quotas for women in assemblies, so a weak agree is inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Soviet autarkic planning fits the idea, but it was a feature of Stalinism rather than of the religion doctrine, so a weak agree.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Marxist–Leninists criticise trade deals as capitalist, so a weak disagree is inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Soviet leaders used both moral and material incentives; adherents lean away from replacing the material altogether.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Lenin ties change to organised class struggle, not small armed groups, but the point is inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though Lenin attacks Tsarist privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Soviet history teaching centred on class struggle and not on a civilisation, so a mild disagree.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Marxist–Leninism condemns colonial tutelage, so the statement is rejected by inference.

patriotic-education.rationale: Soviet schools taught Soviet patriotism, so a weak agree; the sources opened are about atheist education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Soviet nationalities policy gave preferences to minorities, so abolition is mildly rejected.

public-money-creation.rationale: State control of money creation fits the planned economy, so a weak agree is inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lenin's view that religion's root persists until capitalism is overthrown implies capitalism does not simply reform, though not explicit.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Marxist–Leninists criticise both imperialism and neo-imperial influence; adherents are split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency theorists favour delinking but Marxist–Leninist states traded within their bloc; split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Lenin used the labour-aristocracy idea, but adherents disagree about its scope, so neutral.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Lenin condemns discrimination on grounds of belief, so private freedom to discriminate is rejected by inference.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Marxist–Leninists treat entrenched rights as bourgeois, so a mild disagree; the sources do not state this.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-imperial doctrine would treat unequal colonial treaties as void; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Marxist–Leninists support elected, recallable officials; inferred, as the atheism sources do not address rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism binds the minority to the majority, so a minority veto is rejected by inference.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The idea of resisting rulers who break constitutional trust fits revolutionary doctrine only weakly; adherents lean mildly agree.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Soviet doctrine makes soviets or assemblies the supreme state organ, so a weak agree.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Soviet science treated animals mainly as resources, so a weak agree only.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Soviet agriculture and research used animals, so a weak agree is inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Lenin calls charity a tool that keeps workers submissive, and the article records him saying religion teaches the rich charity to justify inequality.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Lenin demands active party struggle, so withdrawal is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Lenin calls religion a spiritual booze that keeps the exploited passive, a close analogue though not about mass culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Lenin treats religion as one way the ruling class keeps workers submissive, but the statement is broader.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Leninist imperialism theory holds that poor countries are drained by rich ones, but it is not in the atheism sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: Internationalist doctrine rejects reserving offices for native-born citizens; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Marxist–Leninist doctrine was divided between Soviet leadership and independent roads, so adherents mildly disagree.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Marxist–Leninism supports bloc aid and trade, so a weak agree for self-reliance is inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Proletarian internationalism opposes irredentist demands, so a mild disagree is inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Marxist–Leninists support class leadership over ethnic leadership, so a mild disagree.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Soviet states treated anti-fascism as foundational, as East Germany did, so a weak agree.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Marxist–Leninists reject equating communism with fascism, so strongly disagree is inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist historians hold that the Civil War was driven by slave-based social relations, so the statement is rejected.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though the Soviets converted churches to other uses.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Marxist–Leninists would focus on class instead of gender-specific attention, so a mild disagree.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Soviet doctrine does not frame violence by gender symmetry, so a mild disagree is inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Marxist–Leninism claims universal laws of historical development, so the statement is mildly rejected.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Marxist–Leninist armies were subordinate to the party, so a guardian role is mildly rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: Soviet doctrine favoured socialising care work over wages for it, so a mild disagree.

filial-duty.rationale: Not covered by the sources; Soviet culture promoted respect for elders, so a weak agree.

office-by-exam.rationale: Marxist–Leninists staffed the state through party nomination, so exam-based selection is mildly rejected.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Socialist states control strategic industry and exclude foreign owners, so adherents agree strongly.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; religious objections to divorce were dismissed in Soviet law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Recallable, mandated delegates are a Commune principle that Lenin endorsed, but not discussed in the atheism sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Marxist–Leninists favour state pensions over private accounts, so strongly disagree; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Soviet land law gave only use rights, so adherents agree; inferred from the parent doctrine.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Soviet assemblies approved budgets formally, so a weak agree is inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Leninist nationalities policy opposed compulsory single languages, so strong disagree; not in the atheism sources.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Socialist states bar private land ownership including by foreigners, so a weak agree.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Marxist–Leninists focus on class not outcome tests for race, so a mild disagree.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Marxist critique of commodity fetishism is balanced by promises of abundance, so adherents are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Soviet Union armed insurgents against hostile governments, so a weak agree is inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Soviet intervention in Hungary and Czechoslovakia fits this, so adherents lean agree weakly.

corporate-influence.rationale: Marxists hold that capital dominates the state, so a weak agree; not covered by the sources opened.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the Soviets restricted foreign links of religious bodies.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Soviet states offered motherhood awards, so a weak agree is inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: No settled view and not covered by the sources, so adherents are split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Soviet constitutions guaranteed the right to work, so adherents agree; the sources opened do not cover it.

democratic-peace.rationale: Leninist theory holds that capitalist democracies go to war, so the claim is mildly rejected.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Marxist–Leninist law was class-based, but Soviet states demanded obedience, so a weak disagree.

non-intervention.rationale: Marxist–Leninists support national sovereignty but also solidarity interventions; weak disagree.

industrial-unions.rationale: Lenin favoured broad class organisation over narrow craft, so a weak agree is inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Lenin insists religious workers be won over without offending them and opposes splitting workers by belief, which counters a conspiracy view.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Soviet states kept registered marriage after a brief 1920s experiment, so a mild disagree.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states restricted information, so a mild disagree.

local-production.rationale: Marxist–Leninist planning favoured industrial concentration over localism, so a mild disagree.

informal-organisation.rationale: Lenin favours a disciplined party, so small informal groups are rejected, but only by inference here.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Soviet doctrine stressed sovereignty over international courts, so a weak agree.

religious-nation.rationale: Lenin demands that the state treat religion as private and make no mention of citizens' faith, so a religion-defined nation is rejected.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Marxist–Leninist internationalism rejects tribute systems, so a mild disagree.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Planned economies redistribute between regions centrally, so a mild disagree.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The distinction between personal and productive property is basic to Marxist–Leninism, but the sources opened do not address it.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents reject it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Marxist–Leninists favour state-run services, so a mixed provider system is rejected.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx calls religion the illusory happiness of the people and the sigh of the oppressed, and Lenin says its roots are social oppression that will fade as exploitation ends.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxists credit capitalism with building productive forces, so a weak agree; not discussed in the atheism sources.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The classical Marxist line that women's emancipation needs economic change, so agree; not in the sources opened.

socialized-care.rationale: Soviet doctrine called for socialising housework and childcare, so a weak agree.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Marxist–Leninists do not promote linguistic purism, so a mild disagree.

treaties-binding.rationale: No settled doctrine and not covered by the sources, so a mild disagree is inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Marxist–Leninists reject small-commune utopianism in favour of state socialism, so disagree.

majority-settlement.rationale: Soviet policy encouraged Russian settlement in other republics, but doctrine formally opposed it, so a mild disagree.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; rejected by adherents.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Marxism rejects religious-tie land claims, so a mild disagree is inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states condemned Nazi crimes, so denial is rejected, though sources opened do not discuss it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Soviet law criminalised it, but the matter is contested among later Marxist–Leninists.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The article records Soviet suppression of religious groups, but general suppression of opposition is not covered.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Lenin condemns laws that persecute people for their belief or disbelief and demands that the state not enforce religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Leninist anti-imperialism rejects colonial exploitation, so strongly disagree, though not stated in these sources.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed directly; religious duty is not a ground for action in Lenin's view.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Lenin demands the state be neutral on religion, so removing rulers for lacking religious law is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Soviet-style direct participation in workplaces and communities is a stated ideal, so a weak agree.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Marxist–Leninists prioritise class over intersectional frames, so a mild disagree.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states historically did not recognise this, so a mild disagree.

assisted-dying.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states did not legalise it and the sources are silent, so a mild disagree.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Marxists treat left and right as class positions, so adherents reject obsolescence.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's early writings, of which the opened essay is part, make alienation central to his critique of capitalist labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Marxist–Leninists treated all religions alike as superstition, so a civilisational incompatibility claim is mildly rejected.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Lenin treats religion as the ruling class's tool and demands a state that does not rest on belief, so authority from God is rejected.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Lenin demands the state ignore citizens' faith and Soviet states kept schools secular, so a weak agree on removing religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not covered by the sources, so a weak agree is inferred from Soviet gender-equality policy.

social-market-economy.rationale: Marxist–Leninists see social-market models as reformist, so a mild disagree.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Marxist–Leninists maintain armies to defend socialism, so strongly disagree.

rich-first.rationale: Marxist–Leninists reject letting some grow rich first, even though China adopted it, so a mild disagree.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states aligned with the Soviet bloc, so neutrality is mildly rejected.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects hereditary rule though North Korea differs, so strongly disagree is inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: State banks, not mutual banks, are the Marxist–Leninist model, so a mild disagree.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-imperialist doctrine opposes IMF conditions, so a weak agree.

property-franchise.rationale: Lenin's programme demanded universal suffrage and attacked property franchise as bourgeois, but not in the atheism sources opened.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Marxist–Leninists have no settled view on ecofeminism, so neutral.

reification.rationale: The idea of commodity fetishism comes from Marx's Capital; the atheism sources opened do not discuss it, so a weak agree.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marx and Lenin held that freedom of the press is hollow under capitalism, though not in the opened religion sources, so a weak agree.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Marxist–Leninists see law as class instrument not independent restraint, so a mild disagree.

racial-franchise.rationale: Lenin demanded equal rights without discrimination, so a racial franchise is strongly rejected by inference.

online-participation.rationale: No settled doctrine and not covered, so neutral.

open-government-data.rationale: Marxist–Leninist states are secretive, so a mild disagree.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Lenin's 1905 demand for equal rights regardless of belief rules out marriage restrictions between faiths.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Lenin opposes dividing people along religious lines, so religious boycotts are rejected.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Marxist–Leninists prefer party-guided councils over random selection, so a mild disagree.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Lenin censures god-building and Christian socialism as deviations from Marxism, though modernising reform is not discussed directly.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Soviet states taught scientific atheism in schools and universities, following Lenin's call for untiring atheist propaganda.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Marxist-Leninist view that private capital controls politics and abolishing it is a precondition of real freedom.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Soviet policy, which criminalised homosexuality and treated it as incompatible with the military.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the doctrine that the state and its coercive organs are needed during the proletarian dictatorship and wither away only under communism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from class rule and one-party leadership, which exclude guaranteed communal shares.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the view that charity and church consolation mask exploitation, and that social provision belongs to the state.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Soviet practice, where leaders held office without limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic centralism, where authority runs through the Party rather than delegable votes.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Soviet disarmament and peace campaigns and the doctrine's faith in rational planning.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; Lenin treated religion as the church's private affair under the state, so internal church offices were of no concern to the state.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the early Soviet legal equality of spouses.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the parent doctrine; communist states restricted voting by citizenship, but internationalist ideology points the other way, so it is split.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism's hostility to the landlord class and support for state control of housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred; the parent doctrine opposes private monopoly, but Soviet practice kept inventors' rights, so it is unresolved.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet Pioneer and Komsomol organisations, which the parent doctrine used for mobilised, ideological youth training.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred; the Soviet bloc itself held nuclear arms, so the parent doctrine has no clean position.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred; anti-imperialism opposes Western bases, but Soviet-bloc states hosted Soviet forces.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources about atheism; inferred from the parent doctrine.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Lenin's Socialism and Religion contrasts those who work all their lives with those who live off the labour of others, and the doctrine holds that income should come from work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred; the parent doctrine accepts revolutionary and defensive violence, so absolute non-killing is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred; Marxist historical materialism treats nations as historical products, not eternal continuities.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred and anachronistic; the Soviet tradition treated sex as biological, though the sources do not address it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred; Marxism-Leninism subordinated women's issues to the class struggle and a single category of working women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred; the doctrine honoured fallen heroes but rejected religious language of sainthood.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Lenin's militant materialism and Marx's critique of religion treat politics as class struggle on a materialist basis, rejecting a spiritual good-versus-evil framing.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which opposes ethnic-cultural centres.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred; the parent doctrine puts the seizure of state power and class struggle before cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: The doctrine rejects God altogether, so the question of male description does not arise cleanly; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Lenin's view is that religion is an illusion to be fought by propaganda, not reformed, so judging texts by women's humanity is inferred to be a non-question.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which rejects privileging a national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred; Soviet policy created ethnic territorial units, but the doctrine also opposed nationalism, so it is split.

independent-unions.rationale: Not covered by the religion texts; inferred from Leninism treating unions as transmission belts of the Party, as in communist states.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism's dictatorship of the proletariat; the sources, which concern religion, do not discuss it.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to public ownership of essential services in communist states.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from Leninist preference for unified soviet power over a divided legislature.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of state ownership; municipal ownership by local communities conflicts with central planning.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from democratic centralism, which subordinates local bodies to the Party centre.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from communist states' policy of drawing women into paid work and standardised wage scales rather than family wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear position follows.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear position follows.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from communist states' total state control of money and finance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from communist states' surveillance and control of communications.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of the party-state and collective over the individual in Marxism-Leninism.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The sources treat religion as an illusion and hold atheism part of the communist worldview, rejecting a spiritual nature of humans.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from democratic centralism, under which central bodies can override regional ones.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; the Soviet record on genetics was mixed, so no clear position follows.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which puts class above race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which treats racial pride as divisive.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism's support for revolutionary and liberation wars beyond mere defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not addressed by the religion-focused sources; Marxism-Leninism defined nations by economy and territory as well as language, so inferred as a mild disagreement with language alone defining a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's demand that religion be a private matter separate from the state, which rules out religion-based political representation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from Soviet-era claims of imperialist subversion; the religion sources do not discuss it.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed in the religion sources; inferred from socialist states' free state education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from the planned-economy preference for state direction over pricing instruments; not addressed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the socialist state's long-term planning and progress ethic.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist insistence on equal roles and class over gender essentialism; not addressed in the sources.

arms-reduction.rationale: Soviet states proclaimed disarmament while building arms; adherents split and the sources do not discuss it, so inferred as neutral.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Lenin published the tsarist secret treaties but Soviet practice kept secrecy; inferred as split, not drawn from the religion sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from state control of foreign trade and finance in Marxist-Leninist economies; not covered in the religion sources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from Leninist doctrine of a centralised state holding the means of force; this audit's sources only cover religion.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's opposition to imperialist wars between states, which he wanted turned into civil war; the audit's religion sources do not address it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism's support for organised labour acting collectively; Soviet unions were party-led, so this is weaker than for social democrats.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: Marxism-Leninism treats wage top-ups as palliatives within capitalism and seeks to abolish wage dependence rather than subsidise it.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet model of a state-planned economy, in which borrowing is a planning decision and not a legally capped one.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from Leninist anti-imperialism, which backs poorer countries against the imperialist economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Core Leninist doctrine holds that revolution must break the bourgeois state apparatus and replace it with new organs of proletarian power; the audit's sources treat the state as an instrument of class rule.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: Marxism-Leninism sets out a scientific plan for socialism under party direction, so it favours one agreed system over open experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from materialist and planned-economy thinking, which does not usually treat nature as priced capital; rarely addressed in the sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: Its materialism and atheism reject the sacred as an illusion, and its internationalism gives class, not nation, priority.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from Soviet-style free or state-funded education and hostility to private debt burdens; not addressed in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's analysis of imperialism and the national question, which treats unequal development between regions or nations as exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Marx's view that the human essence is the ensemble of social relations, and the Soviet aim of forming a new person; the religion sources are indirect on this.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from Soviet practice, in which broadcasting was owned and directed by the party-state, so independence from government is not an adherent aim.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The doctrine treats religion as an illusion produced by exploitation, so no religion expresses a spiritual truth, and it rejects the claim that they share one.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism's state-directed agrarian policy and collectivisation; the atheism doctrine itself says nothing on it.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Soviet practice of building and keeping nuclear arms against rivals; the sources do not discuss it.

workers-own-party.rationale: Lenin held that the workers' party must be the class-conscious vanguard and carry on materialist propaganda as its own affair.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hostility to harmful custom and religious practice and its stated commitment to women's equality.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist commitment to women's legal equality and abolition of religious and customary rules that disadvantage them.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question the doctrine never addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from its preference for state planning and public ownership over private lawsuits between property owners.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to religious and traditional authority and its demand that church and clergy have no public role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred; the doctrine subordinates individual liberty to the party and class struggle but the sources say nothing on environmental priority.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from Soviet reliance on fixed state penalties and party-directed justice; the sources do not discuss sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed by the atheism doctrine; Soviet practice mixed promotion of Russian with support for national languages.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism, where trade unions served the party and state, and membership was treated as normal for workers.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the parent doctrine, which saw bourgeois electoral rules as class tools rather than integrity safeguards.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Lenin asked that religion be a private matter in relation to the state, with no church privileged, though in practice states pursued official atheism.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism, which treated bourgeois electoral democracy as class rule and defined democracy by the working class holding power.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the parent doctrine, which attacked religious sexual morality, though Lenin himself disliked sexual licence.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism's party-state control of information and priority on order against enemies.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the parent doctrine, which sought a planned economy with state provision rather than market-linked cash payments.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the parent doctrine; Soviet Russia gave women the vote in 1917.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Engels and Lenin treated religion as a tool of exploitation that keeps the oppressed in their place, women included.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism's rejection of biological racial hierarchies in favour of class analysis.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from Soviet practice such as the Zhenotdel women's department and the party's stated goal of women's emancipation.

missingStatements.text: The state should actively promote atheism through its schools and public education.
missingStatements.rationale: Soviet states taught scientific atheism in schools and universities, following Lenin's call for untiring atheist propaganda.

missingStatements.text: Churches and other religious bodies should receive no public funds.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin's 1905 programme demands that the state give no money to any church or religious association.

notes: Most answers outside religion are inferred from the parent Marxism–Leninism and are low confidence, so the profile has few stated positions. Practice also differed from Lenin's formula that religion is private: Soviet and Albanian policy went to closure and persecution.
